verdict.rationale: Sentry's source is publicly hosted on GitHub and early community comments praise its 'fully open source nature' for letting users read the code directly, but other community evidence shows the license changed and is no longer straightforwardly open (a user explicitly says they 'refuse to rely on closed-source software' and switched away, and a competitor was built as a non-vendor-locked alternative), indicating the current license is not a clean open-source grant. Missing for 10: an explicit current license statement (e.g. OSI-approved license text) and confirmation the license controversy has been resolved.
